title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is an irregular list of runs with one long periodic block in it, (001111111001)^3766 at the left end at step 882,788,555 (and its translation (011011101011)^2687 at the right end), which grows steadily while the rest stays irregular. Measured, not proved. Halting needs E on a 1, entered only from D on a 0; E has always found a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 51,938 cells have been visited and 35,128 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.663). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.473).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rules of the leftward sweep in B: it turns (01)^n into (11)^n (2 steps per copy) and (011)^n into (001)^n (5 steps per copy).

claims.title: A periodic block in an irregular list
claims.text: At the last left extension before 109 steps (step 882,788,555) the tape is E>0 1^17 0010 1^3 0 (01)^3 1^4 00 1^5 (001)^4 1^8 … (001111111001)^3766 00 (10011)^3 …: runs of 1s of length 3a+1 (7,550 of 7,582) separated by 00 (7,574 of 7,581 runs of 0s have length 2), and a periodic block of 3,766 copies of 1^7 00 1 00. At the last right extension (step 999,852,606) the same block reads (011011101011)^2687 followed by (01)^1608.

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when E reads a 1, and E is entered only from D reading a 0 (D0 → 1LE). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps D reads a 0 297,649 times, always with a 0 to its left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The periodic block is a clean counter, but the irregular rest of the list, where a halt would have to happen, is not understood.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1RF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine's tape is an irregular list of runs with one long, regular, growing block in the middle. This page shows them and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 51,938 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A regular block in an irregular list
html: At the left end the tape is runs of 1s separated by 0 0, mostly of length 1, 4, 7, 10, … (3a + 1):

In the middle sits one long regular block, 0 0 1^7 0 0 1 repeated 3,766 times, that grows as the machine runs; around it the list shows no order. At the right end the same block is written in another code, (011011101011)^2687.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in E reading a 1, and E is entered only from D reading a 0 (moving left). So a halt needs D on a 0 with a 1 to its left. In the first 3·106 steps D reads a 0 297,649 times and the cell to its left is always 0. Open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.663). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.473).
After 109 steps the tape spans 51,938 cells (14,411 left of the start, 21,766 right), with a density of 1s of 0.676.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1RF: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1RF: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1RF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror

family: growing periodic block inside an irregular list
summary: Both sides grow by sweeps; the tape is an irregular list with one long periodic block inside it (the word 1^7 00 1 00 repeated, 3,766 times at 8.8·10^8 steps) that grows steadily.
